Five months since the start of the Middle East crisis, continued disruptions in global fuel and fertilizer markets, coupled with forecasts of a strong El Niño event, have increased uncertainty in global agricultural production. As crops enter critical growth stages, the risk of below CPI data is from Trading Economics. Bhutan data is from April 2026 and Afghanistan and Cambodia data is from May 2026. average rainfall linked to El Niño pose a substantial threat to production at a time when elevated input costs have already limited farmers' ability to invest in additional irrigation or crop protection measures.

COST OF THE FOOD BASKET AND INFLATION IN ASIA PACIFIC

Increasing food prices continue to pressure household purchasing power. Myanmar has experienced the sharpest increase, with the cost of the food basket rising by 20% compared to pre-crisis levels, with Cambodia and Pakistan both approaching double digits. Tajikistan food prices have dropped, likely thanks to seasonal harvests and a relatively strong USD/TJK exchange rate, helping contain import costs. Looking at overall consumer prices, Fiji and Sri Lanka show notable increases in headline CPI, with prices more than 6% higher than pre-crisis levels. Fiji’s reliance on imported goods makes it vulnerable to global price fluctuations, while Sri Lanka is facing high energy prices passing through into other sectors
